primitives.name: Confidence Score
primitives.verbatim_quote: --## Confidence Score — Rules The confidence score (0–100) measures how strongly the evidence supports the pick direction.
primitives.assumptions: (1) Scores are bounded; (2) They reflect posterior belief given observed data; (3) Higher scores indicate stronger support.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Scores below the floor threshold are clamped to zero.

layer2.mapping: In GSI, this maps to a Bayesian posterior probability after updating on market signals. In GSE, it serves as a threshold for triggering high-confidence actions, with fallback to lower-confidence alternatives when the score drops.
layer2.telemetry: Average confidence score of settled picks, segmented by model version.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge is balancing informativeness with robustness under uncertainty. The primitives formalize this trade-off: the evidence chain ensures verifiability, the confidence score quantifies strength, risk annotation controls exposure, and the tier gate manages access. This structure mirrors conformal prediction in GSI, where the goal is valid predictive sets regardless of model misspecification. In GSE, it enables safe navigation of state spaces by preventing high-risk transitions. Failure occurs when any primitive breaks: an incomplete chain leads to ignorance, low confidence invites overfitting, unchecked risk causes catastrophic decisions, and improper tiering leaks sensitive information. To prevent these, we enforce duality conditions: every pick must have a corresponding testable hypothesis, every action must have a fallback under high risk, and every layer must maintain separation of concerns.
